claim_or_location: LaBelle values stored as layers['tpm'] and described as TPM; note claims 'P9 is a 10x library distributed as per-cell CPM (nCount_RNA = 1e6)'
evidence: All three GSE227983 tables are log2(TPM/10+1), not linear TPM: first 6 columns of tumor_ss2 have column sums 8,257-12,624, max 8.0-8.65, 100% fractional non-zeros; immune_ss2 sums 4,183-5,391; immune_tenx (P9 source) sums 3,661-6,177, max 7.6-9.0. Inverting (2^x-1)*10 gives 2.0e5-3.0e5 per cell (TPM over a gene-filtered table). qc_per_sample.csv median_counts for LaBelle SS2 samples = 4,823-9,527 and for P9 = 3,244, versus exactly 1e6 for every Filbin sample.
impact_on_conclusions: The Phase 2 deliverable mislabels a log-scale matrix as TPM and the note is factually wrong (nCount is ~3e3, not 1e6). Downstream phases detected the scale heuristically (cnv.py / 10_prepare_queries.py: rowmax<30 => log2), so atlas conclusions are not affected, but any consumer of labelle.qc.h5ad['tpm'] without that heuristic would be off by orders of magnitude.
recommendation: Rename the layer (e.g. 'log2_tpm10') or invert to linear TPM at ingest; record the scale in uns and var; correct the note (P9 CPM/1e6 claim) and the qc_report 'median counts' column for TPM cohorts.

evidence: obs of okada.qc.h5ad: 1734_pons n_genes median 321 (IQR 249-452), n_counts median 351, 6,665 (43.8%) fail low_genes; passing nuclei have median 427 genes / 468 UMI, versus 971-2,805 genes in the other 21 Okada samples (next lowest 586_pons 971). claim_or_location: Notes: Liu has 'two annotations in the deposit' (32,617 / 23,686 genes) and only 'Filbin / LaBelle TPM tables contain no MT- genes'; Liu frozen nuclei are QC'd with the smartseq2 class (mito < 20%)
evidence: gene_harmonisation.csv: Liu raw files come in three annotations: 23,686 genes (16 samples, 4,007 unmapped), 32,617 (20 samples, 1,749 unmapped) and 55,765 (6 samples, 22,216 unmapped). All 16 samples on the 23,686-gene annotation (5,375 cells, all author_prep = frozen_nuclei) have pct_mito identically 0 for every cell (max 0.0), i.e. the annotation lacks MT- genes and the mito filter is inoperative (visible as flat markers in qc_violin_liu.png). Among frozen nuclei that do carry MT genes, 138 of 680 passing nuclei (20.3%) have 5-20% mito and would fail the project's own nuclei rule.
impact_on_conclusions: QC is heterogeneous within the Liu cohort (mito-filtered vs unfiltered samples; nuclei judged by the cell threshold). Liu is projection-only, so reference models are unaffected, but Liu-based comparisons (fresh vs frozen, pediatric vs adult) carry a QC confound that the notes do not disclose.
recommendation: State the three annotations and MT-gene absence in the notes; add a per-sample 'mt_genes_present' column to qc_per_sample.csv; apply the nuclei mito rule (or author_prep-aware rule) to frozen nuclei where MT genes exist.

claim_or_location: 'per-study medians 0.19 ScPCA to 0.63 Zang'; 'called 0 doublets in most samples'; predicted_doublet_fixed (score > 0.25) 'gives 0.1-2.6% per study'
evidence: qc_per_sample.csv (95 UMI samples with a threshold): per-study median auto-thresholds are ScPCA 0.19, DeSisto 0.28, multiome 0.38, Zang 0.38, scRNA 0.39, Okada 0.42, Collot 0.51 (no study at 0.63); 36/96 samples (37.5%) have 0 auto-called doublets (median per-sample rate 0.0003). Fixed-threshold pooled rates: DeSisto 0.08%, Zang 0.50%, Collot 1.06%, Okada 2.55% (claim verified). These are 3-10x below the expected 10x multiplet rate (~0.8% per 1,000 loaded cells; e.g. 586_pons has 23.7k nuclei). expected_doublet_rate is fixed at 0.06 regardless of cells loaded and the 0.25 cut-off is arbitrary.
impact_on_conclusions: Doublets are likely under-called in the atlas input (which excludes predicted_doublet_fixed); residual heterotypic doublets can appear as hybrid malignant/TME states. Two descriptive numbers in the note are wrong.
recommendation: Correct the note; calibrate doublet calls (scDblFinder or per-sample expected rate from cell number) before state discovery; report per-sample expected vs called rates.

claim_or_location: 'LaBelle SS2 cells come from two tables (tumour, immune) with different gene lists (14,642 vs 19,357) -> zero-filled union'
evidence: Within each of samples P1-P8 the tumour and immune SS2 tables are concatenated with join='inner' (gene_harmonisation.csv: n_input_genes 14,621 for P1-P8, 19,357 for P9); the immune cells therefore lose 4,736 measured genes before the across-sample outer join. var: 14,487 genes measured in all samples, 4,625 measured only in P9.
impact_on_conclusions: Immune SS2 cells of LaBelle lack genes that were measured; minor for a projection-only cohort but contrary to the documented rule.
recommendation: Use join='outer' with fill_value=0 within samples too, and track measured genes per table.

claim_or_location: Per-sample max genes = 99.5th percentile of n_genes
evidence: The quantile is taken over all deposited barcodes (including empty/low-count ones) and applied on top of author caps: in Okada (authors already enforced nFeature < 5000) 849 nuclei fail only high_genes; in Jessa 0 author-QC cells fail only high_genes (the top 0.5% are all non-author barcodes). impact_on_conclusions: Small (<=0.5% per sample) but systematic removal of the highest-complexity cells (often cycling) in studies without an author cap.
recommendation: Replace with a doublet-informed or MAD-based upper bound, or document that 0.5% is intentional.
